Initial work focused on finalizing system definition and pivoting from a liquid hydrogen to liquid nitrogen-based test platform to reduce cost of system components and lead time of critical components. A preliminary logic flow for the control system was constructed. A system PID was created to establish a relationship between process gas components, sensors, and system ID tags, along with a controls and reference schematic (Figure 33). 1. Figure 33. Significant Accomplishments and Conclusions: This project successfully showed multiple paths for autonomous fueling of vehicles including: • Designed and demonstrated autonomous fueling of a materials handling truck with gaseous hydrogen using a low-cost robotic arm. • Designed and carried out preliminary demonstrations of autonomous fueling of a commercial fuel cell vehicle through the building of a robotic fixture with real hydrogen components including nozzle and hose. • Developed the baseline technology for autonomous fueling with liquid hydrogen. 9. Path Forward: A baseline understanding of the key elements of robotic refueling have been demonstrated. For the materials handling application, robotic refueling may become feasible in autonomous warehouses.
